palPh: Open a module, note or action…
r_memory: Library files and notes, clustered by project. Lights up when Claude reads a file.
r_planning: Task lists and plans. Lights up when Claude updates a task list.
r_execution: Terminal commands and file changes. Lights up on commands and edits.
r_research: Web sources. Lights up on web search or fetch.
r_workflows: Skills and routines. Lights up when Claude uses a skill.
r_connectors: MCP servers, plugins and external apps. Lights up on connector calls.
r_subagents: Subagent activity. Lights up when Claude starts a subagent.
libGrow: The brain grows with your library: the more files are linked, the larger and denser it gets. No files: a small, sparse seed.
demoNote: Demo events. Real events come from Claude Code hooks (Phase 3).
privacyD: Hides paths and names on screen
evoTxt: The change log of NEURAL OS itself, not of Claude and not of your projects. It shows what changed in the app and when: versions, features, connectors, index migrations, the readiness rule and the installed hooks.
secTxt: Every change NEURAL OS made to Claude Code files, each with undo.
graphTxt: Your library as a graph: notes, files, projects and Claude sessions, and how they link. Filter it, focus it, compare it.
planTxt: Task lists Claude wrote, as observed.
wfTxt: Skills and routines Claude used, as observed.
modelTxt: Shown only when Claude Code reports it.
regionOther: Unmapped events use a neutral pathway.
bodyTxt: Below the brain runs the spinal cord. Each connector is wired in by its own nerve from the cord; a new connector grows out as a new nerve. Missing or sign-in connectors stay dimmed.
attnNone: Nothing needs your attention right now.
regActHint: Counted from the events observed in this session.
actHint: Click an event to light up its region in the brain.
evoNot: NEURAL OS never changes itself. Every change comes from an update or from you; changes to Claude Code files can be undone under Security.
ev_rule: Readiness rule v1 added to CLAUDE.md
cmpHint: Shared nodes are notes and files linked from both projects.
w1: Obsidian stores what you know. NEURAL OS also shows you, live, what Claude does with your knowledge: which notes it reads, what it changes and which tools it uses.
w1a: Link your Obsidian vault, import folders or drop in single files: notes, code, PDFs, images. Your brain grows with your library.
w1b: See live which files Claude Code reads and edits, which tools, skills and subagents it uses, and which connectors are ready.
w1c: The library is a normal folder of Markdown files. Claude Code can read it like any folder you allow it to, or you hand it a context pack. NEURAL OS sends nothing by itself.
w1not: What it is not: NEURAL OS has no AI of its own. It never gives Claude tasks and never changes your original files. It only shows what is really observable.
w2: Imported copies, your notes and NEURAL OS metadata live here. Plain Markdown files: any Markdown tool, including Obsidian, can open them.
w3: Optional. You can do this later at any time.
imp_vault_d: Stays where it is, read-only by default. Best for large or live folders.
imp_folder_d: Copies files into the library. Originals are never changed.
w4: Optional. NEURAL OS adds silent hooks to your user-level Claude Code settings so it can see tool events. This is the exact change:
w5: Optional. A short rule that asks Claude to check its tools before larger tasks. It is added to your global CLAUDE.md:
w6: Your brain grows with your library and lights up when Claude works. Everything else opens from the dock on the left or with Ctrl/Cmd+K.
w_example: Example. The exact hook names are checked against the official Claude Code documentation before they are built in (Phase 0).
backupNote: A backup is made before anything is written. Undo at any time under Security.
mode_copy_d: For single files and small folders. The original is never moved or changed.
mode_link_d: For folders over 1 GB or 5,000 files, or folders that change often. Only path, index and metadata are stored.
dupes: {n} files are already in the library (same content). They will be skipped.
editNote: Before saving, NEURAL OS checks that the file did not change on disk and keeps a backup of every version.
drop_s: Files are copied or linked, never moved. You choose in the next step.
diff_title: Change to a Claude Code file
diff_intro: NEURAL OS wants to write to this file. Nothing is written without your approval.
cf_intro: {file} changed on disk while you were editing it (Claude, 14:22). Nothing has been overwritten.
cf_backup: Whichever you choose, the other version is kept as a backup.
ocrNote: OCR text, generated locally. Not source text.
nameOnlyD: Large binary file: only name, type, size and dates are indexed.
claudeMdNote: Read-only by default. Editing follows the consent rule: backup, diff, undo.
packIntro: One Markdown file you hand to Claude in Claude Code yourself. NEURAL OS does not send it anywhere.
packSaved: Demo: would save context-pack.md in the library.
removeQ: Removes only the library copy and its derived data. The original file is never touched.
sessHint: Mute: recorded, not animated. Off: not recorded.
clearQ: Delete the stored activity history? Library files and notes are not affected. This cannot be undone.
roProj: NEURAL OS stays read-only toward your Claude project files.
projHint: Projects only group things inside NEURAL OS. Your original project folders are not changed.
unassignedD: Events and files without a reliable project.
qD: Low: fewer effects for weak GPUs
dockHideD: Appears when the mouse reaches the left edge
modsD: Turned-off modules disappear from the dock.
moveD: Guided move of the library folder (demo).
realLibEmpty: Still empty. Drop files onto the window or add them here.
imp_res: {a} imported, {b} already in the library, {c} failed
autoLinkD: New files go into the matching project and are linked by fixed rules: wikilinks, mentions, same folder, similar name. Off: links stay suggestions.
unlinkD: NEURAL OS forgets its index and links for “{name}”. The folder and its files stay exactly as they are.
liveWatch: Changes are picked up live, at the latest after 10 minutes. “Rescan” picks them up now.
colorsD: Colourful: every region, nerve and project gets its own colour
tlD: Each bar is one month: when your files were last changed. Click a month to light up its files in the brain.
tlEmpty: No files of your own yet. Add files or link a folder and your timeline appears here.
colorByD: What your files in the brain are coloured by
turningD: The brain turns slowly while you do nothing
formD: Pulls your files out of the brain into one cloud per group (colour by)
formNone: Once you have files of your own
regLabelsD: As a colour list at the side (clean) or right inside the brain
nOrphansD: Files without a link are hard to find again later. A [[link]] in a related note helps.
nYouD: Not available yet. Once the live monitor receives real Claude events, this shows what you wrote yourself and what Claude changed. Nothing is estimated.
imp_vaultHint: This is an Obsidian vault. Linking is recommended: it stays where it is, is only read and changes show up right away. Copying would store it twice.
linkColorD: By brain region (Memory, Workflows, …) or like the files
cMissing: File not found. It may have been moved.
cNoPreview: No preview for this file type yet.
monIntro: Connect Claude Code so NEURAL OS shows real events: which files Claude reads and changes, which tools run, and every change with before and after. No prompts, no output, no thoughts.
monConsentTxt: NEURAL OS adds its own hook entries to your Claude Code settings. Everything else in the file stays as it is. This is the exact change:
monRemoveTxt: NEURAL OS removes only its own hook entries. This is the exact change:
monConsentNote: A backup is made first. The hooks are silent and cost no tokens. Only for file changes Claude waits briefly (about 50 ms) so the previous version can be saved. When NEURAL OS is closed, nothing happens. Applies to new Claude Code sessions.
monRemoveNote: A backup is made first. The saved history stays.
monBadSettings: Your Claude Code settings are not valid JSON, so NEURAL OS does not change the file.
monNoNode: Node.js was not found. The hooks need Node.js (nodejs.org).
monInstalled: Claude Code connected. New sessions appear here.
monFailed: That did not work. Nothing was changed.
monNoSess: No session yet. Start Claude Code and it appears here.
monLiveHint: Only observed events from Claude Code hooks. Nothing here is guessed.
monHistHint: History of the last 30 days, stored on this computer.
chNone: No changes yet. Once Claude Code is connected and changes a file, you see before and after here.
chRestoreNote: Restore is only offered for folders where you allowed editing. Your files stay untouched.
chHint: Every change Claude makes to a text file, with before and after.
monNotesHint: After each answer NEURAL OS writes a note about the session into your library (folder Sessions): project, time, files read and changed, tools. Observed facts only, no summary.
monOutdated: The hook setup is outdated (for example a Node path that changes on updates). Reconnect so events keep arriving.
demoPartTip: Claude activity and your library are real. Connectors, models and workflows are still demo data.
ruleIntro: A rule for Claude Code: before larger tasks Claude checks that all needed plugins and connectors are there and asks you before anything is added. At the end of a task Claude writes one "SESSION-NOTE: …" line that NEURAL OS adds to the session note. With “Context for Claude” set up, Claude also looks into your notes and the last session first on larger tasks and names the notes it used. The rule applies to all your projects and works without NEURAL OS too.
ruleConsentTxt: NEURAL OS adds a marked block to your global Claude Code instructions. Text outside the block stays as it is. This is the exact change:
ruleRemoveTxt: NEURAL OS removes only the marked block. This is the exact change:
ruleNote: A backup is made first. Applies to new Claude Code sessions.
ruleInstalled: Rule installed. New Claude sessions follow it.
ruleBroken: The file has the start of the NEURAL OS block but no end, so NEURAL OS does not change it.
rcNone: No report yet. It appears here once Claude checks before a larger task.
rcNoRule: Install the rule and Claude's reports appear here.
rcHint: Only reports Claude wrote itself (line "READINESS:"). Nothing here is guessed.
wBackupReal: Nothing is written before you click "Open NEURAL OS", and a backup is made first. Remove it any time with one click: hooks in Activity, rule in Connectors.
ctxIntro: Claude can ask NEURAL OS for context, for example: "What did we do last time in this project?" NEURAL OS answers from your notes and session notes, without AI, always with sources. The notes light up in the brain.
ctxConsentTxt: NEURAL OS registers its context server with the official Claude Code command (for all your projects). This is the exact command:
ctxRemoveTxt: NEURAL OS unregisters the context server with this official command:
ctxNote: A backup of ~/.claude.json is made first. Applies to new Claude Code sessions. The server runs locally only, reads only and has no network connection.
ctxManual: If you have a terminal where “claude” works, this also works: copy the command and paste it there. It also works in Windows PowerShell.
ctxOnHint: Claude sees the tools search_notes, recent_sessions, context_pack and list_projects.
ctxInstalled: Context server set up. New Claude sessions can use it.
ctxFlash: Claude took {n} notes from NEURAL OS
setupIntro: Set up NEURAL OS step by step. A tick means: done on this computer. You can stop anytime and continue later.
setupAll: All set. NEURAL OS is now your AI's long-term memory.
setupNA: Cannot be checked in the demo
setup_nodeD: A small program Claude Code uses to talk to NEURAL OS. Download the "LTS" version from nodejs.org and install it with the default settings. Then restart NEURAL OS.
setup_notesD: Drag files or a folder into the window, or click "Link folder…" under Memory → Library. An Obsidian vault is only read, never changed.
setup_connectD: Click "Connect Claude Code…" under Activity → Live. You see exactly what will be written to your Claude Code settings first. A backup is made, and removing it takes one click.
setup_sessionD: Open Claude Code as usual and give it a small task. As soon as Claude reads or changes something, the brain lights up and the session appears under Activity.
setup_ruleD: Click "Install rule…" under Connectors. Claude then checks before big tasks that all tools are there, and writes a short summary for your session note at the end of a task.
setup_contextD: Click "Set up for Claude…" under Connectors → "Context for Claude". Then Claude can look things up in your notes itself. Restart Claude Code once afterwards.
setup_tryD: Ask Claude in a new session: "What did we do last time in this project?" When Claude fetches notes, they light up in the brain. Then you are done.
cExtracted: Text from the {t} file, without layout. The file itself stays unchanged.
cExtractedP: Text from the {t} file ({n} pages), without layout. The file itself stays unchanged.
cNoText: No text was found in this file (for example a scanned PDF).
bShareD: Saves your notes and files with their links and projects as one .brain file. NEURAL OS uploads nothing: share the file yourself, for example via MEGA or another download link.
bMissing: {n} files were missing on disk and were skipped.
bNone: No other brain yet. Import a .brain file someone sent you.
bRemoveD: “{name}” is deleted from NEURAL OS. Your own notes and notes you already copied stay.
bReadOnly: Other brains are read-only. You can copy single notes into your brain; the source stays unchanged.
bNoBridge: No matching note in your brain.
lesIntro: At the end of a task, Claude writes in one line what it learned. You decide what counts: lessons you keep are given to Claude next time in this project through the context server. That way Claude improves over time, without training.
lesRuleOld: The lesson book needs readiness rule v3. Update it under Connectors → Readiness rule.
lesNeedCtx: So that Claude also fetches the lessons, set up “Context for Claude” under Connectors.
lesDelD: The lesson is deleted from the lesson book. Claude will not get it any more.
lesNone: No lessons for this project yet.
lesNoProject: No lessons yet. As soon as Claude finishes a task with rule v3, they show up here, per project folder.
lesOwnPh: e.g. always write comments in German
lesObsHint: From real events in this project, not guessed. Claude gets them as hints.
lesNoted: Claude noted a lesson. Review it under Activity → Lesson book.
edReadonly: This folder (“{f}”) is read-only. NEURAL OS changes nothing there until you turn on editing for the folder.
edEnableT: Turn on editing for this folder?
edEnableD: NEURAL OS may then change Markdown and text files in “{f}” when you edit them in the editor. Before every save it checks whether the file was changed in the meantime (for example by Claude or Obsidian) and keeps the previous text as a version. Other files are never written. You can turn it off at any time.
edConflictT: The note was changed in the meantime.
edConflictD: Someone else (for example Claude or Obsidian) changed the file while you were writing. Your change is not saved yet.
edCmpHint: Red: only in the changed file. Green: only in your text.
edMineCopied: The other text is taken over. Your text is on the clipboard.
edNoVer: No earlier versions yet. Before every save NEURAL OS keeps the previous text.
edVerHint: The last 50 versions are kept. Restoring can be undone too.
edRestoreD: The note gets the text of this version. The current text is kept as a version first.
edWhyErr_type: only Markdown and text can be edited
edFolderTip: Whether NEURAL OS may change notes in this folder
mdMermaidErr: This diagram could not be drawn; its text stays above.
edSessionRo: NEURAL OS rewrites session notes after every Claude session, so they cannot be edited here; changes would be lost.
menHint: Notes that write this name (or an alias) as plain text, without a [[link]].
menCapped: Only the first {n} notes were searched.
menLinked: Linked. The old text is kept in the versions.
edRenameHint: Links like [[Old name]] in editable notes are updated too (each with a version). Read-only notes stay unchanged.
edRenamedRo: {n} read-only notes still link the old name.
edRenamedAmb: Links not updated: another file has the same name.
edWhyErr_exists: a file with this name already exists there
edWhyErr_conflict: the note just changed, please try again
rtNone: Your notes have no tags yet (#tag in the text or tags: in the properties).
rtHint: All tags from your notes. Click one to see its notes.
fsHint: Searches names and text of all notes, including PDF and Word text. Every word must occur.
cvBad: This canvas file could not be read.
baseBad: This base file could not be read.
baseType: The “{t}” view is shown as a table here.
baseSkipped: NEURAL OS cannot evaluate these parts yet. Filters among them were left out, so the table may show more notes than Obsidian:
exclTip: Leave folders or files of this folder out of NEURAL OS
exclD: One pattern per line. Without / it matches any name (e.g. Imports or *.png), with / a path from this folder (e.g. Studio/Imports/). The files themselves stay unchanged, they are only left out of NEURAL OS.
hlHint: Just a report: NEURAL OS changes nothing here. Click a note to open it.
agIntro: Your agents, their handoffs, grades and open questions, read from your own notes. NEURAL OS changes nothing there and adds nothing made up.
agNone: Nothing found yet. NEURAL OS looks for notes in a folder named “Agents”, handoffs in a folder named “Handoffs” (or notes with lines like FROM: … TO: … STATUS: …), a “Scorecard” note with a table, “Learnings” and “Owner Questions” or “Open questions”. Claude Code subagents show up here once the live connection sees some.
agGradeT: Average of {n} grades in your scorecard
agHint: Click to open the note. Status and grades are taken from your notes as written; where one is missing it says “no status”.
lesNotesD: Learnings that you or your agents wrote down in notes. Take one over and it becomes your lesson in the lesson book, so NEURAL OS hands it to Claude.
grIntro: What Claude Code may do without asking, where it asks and what is denied, plus which hooks run. View only: NEURAL OS changes nothing here.
grEmpty: No own rules, Claude Code uses its defaults.
grHint: Order per the Claude Code docs: denied before ask before allow; admin settings before local project settings before project settings before your own. Projects show up once Claude has worked there.
rcToast: While you were away: Claude worked in {n} sessions (Activity → Live)
rcSince: Since {d}: {n} sessions, {t} tool steps, {f} failed, {c} files changed.
rcNoSummary: No summary from Claude (needs the readiness rule v2 or later).
awHint: Only what the hooks observed plus Claude's own SESSION-NOTE lines. NEURAL OS does not store prompts or tool output.
agPhasesHint: Tasks = ticked boxes in the phase note. Handoffs = handoff notes that link to the phase. If the status says “todo” while handoffs exist, the note is probably out of date.
agPropsHint: From your “Prompt Proposals” note. Nothing is applied unless you do it yourself.
mcHint: Read from ~/.claude.json and the .mcp.json of projects Claude worked in. Only name, type and program or host are shown, never keys or environment variables.
ovToast: Heads-up: two Claude sessions are changing {f}
ovTitle: {n} files were changed by two sessions close together in the last 24 hours
ovHint: Only a hint: NEURAL OS blocks nothing. Check “Changes” to see whether the sessions overwrote each other.
frIntro: What came in lately, what changed last and which notes may be out of date.
frStaleD: Claude read it {n}×, last changed {d}, linked files are newer
frStaleNone: None. A note shows up here once Claude has read it at least twice while files it links to changed later.
rescanTip: Check the whole folder now (new, changed and removed files)
lookD: Particles: soft dots through the whole brain, no lines. Web: dots on the surface with all links.
ovIntro: The brain shows your files as dots. When Claude Code works, the places Claude reads or changes light up. Here you see at a glance what is going on and where to find things.
ovNoneNow: No Claude Code session is working right now. As soon as you use Claude, it shows up here.
ovGlowD: Claude is using this file right now
whMemory: Your files, search, timeline, tags, sharing brains
whActivity: What Claude does, changes, lesson book, agents
whConnectors: Connect Claude, context, rule, MCP servers
goal_notesD: Link a vault or folder, read-only
goal_watchD: See what Claude Code reads and changes
goal_memoryD: Claude looks things up in your notes itself
goal_appsD: Check automatically which programs you have and what Claude can already use
appsNone: None of the known programs found (Roblox Studio, GitHub, Blender, OBS, Figma, Obsidian).
appsNotYet: installed, Claude cannot use it yet
appsHint: NEURAL OS only checks whether the programs are installed in their usual places and reads your Claude Code list of MCP servers. Nothing is installed or sent. “Guide” opens the connector's page in the browser.
vaultsNone: No Obsidian vault found. Just pick a folder.
vaultsHint: Found via Obsidian's own list. Linking means: NEURAL OS only reads the folder, changes nothing and sees new files right away.
ctxWhyTitle: Why it does not work with one click
ctxWhy: NEURAL OS did not find Claude Code on this computer, neither as the “claude” command nor inside the Claude desktop app. Without Claude Code, NEURAL OS cannot register itself with Claude. To fix it: install Claude Code (Claude desktop app or command line), open it once, then click “Set up for Claude…” here again.
ctxFailOut: Claude Code answered with an error. This is the message:
syncD: Same brain on several devices: Claude sessions, history, changes and the lesson book travel through your own cloud folder. NEURAL OS uploads nothing itself; your cloud app does that.
syncNoCloud: No cloud folder found (Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud, Dropbox, MEGA). Choose your cloud folder yourself.
syncNotesHint: Notes and files travel by themselves when your vault is in the cloud folder and linked on both devices.
syncThisD: Its name on your other devices
syncMissing: The sync folder is not there right now (cloud app off or drive disconnected). NEURAL OS syncs again once it is back.
syncNoPeers: No other device yet. On the other device, choose the same cloud folder in NEURAL OS.
syncOffToast: Sync is off. Data already synced stays.
